results.title: A study on stochastic degradation process models under different types of failure Thresholds - ScienceDirect
results.content: Stochastic degradation process models are developed in terms of cumulative degradation signals of systems under three types of thresholds including alarm line and two different failure thresholds. [34] proposed a degradation model with respect to the separated-stage and Gamma process and obtained the real-time reliability. [22] developed a multi-stage degradation model to capture the degradation process with change points and discussed the real-time reliability evaluation and parameter's estimation of a two-stage model named as change-point Gamma and Wiener process in detail. In this paper, we shall develop two degradation models considering two failure criteria, i.e., the above three types of thresholds are considered in the system reliability analysis at the same time. Compared with existing works, our main contributions are: (1) In two-stage degradation processes, we have not only considered the alarm line and the failure threshold, but also considered the duration of degradation value exceeding the alarm line but not reaching the failure threshold; (2) Two degradation models including Wiener-Gamma degradation model and Gamma-Gamma degradation model are developed. After the change-point or the degradation value is greater than the alarm line, the degradation process is regarded as another age-dependent Gamma process; (3) The closed-form expressions of the system reliability are presented, where the system reliability is defined as the probability that the degradation signals do not exceed a failure threshold and the duration of degradation value exceeding the alarm line but not reaching the failure threshold is less than the duration threshold. In each stage, we use a diffusion process (for example, the Wiener process or the Gamma process) to model the cumulative degradation. In this section, we will propose a degradation model considering alarm line, failure threshold and duration threshold at the same time. In this paper, we introduce new models based on a two stage degradation process in which two different failure criteria are used to define the system reliability; that is, a system is regarded as working normally only when the following two conditions are all satisfied: the degradation signals do not exceed a given failure threshold and the duration of exceeding the alarm line is less than a given duration threshold. ### Reliability analysis for a Wiener degradation process model under changing failure thresholds.

results.title: Tailoring Robustness Tests for Biomedical Foundation Models
results.content: # Tailoring Robustness Tests for Biomedical Foundation Models. Biomedical foundation models are increasingly being integrated into healthcare, but their evaluation methods often fail to reflect real-world conditions. An analysis of more than 50 biomedical models revealed that almost one third included no robustness testing and many relied only on cross-dataset consistency, which offers limited insight when the links between datasets are unclear. Foundation models differ from earlier predictive systems because users can steer behaviour at inference through in-context learning, instruction following, tool use and prompting. Among more than 50 biomedical foundation models examined, 31.4% reported no robustness assessment, 33.3% used consistency across multiple datasets as the primary signal and only small fractions evaluated on shifted data, synthetic data or external sites. For example, summarisation or report generation may shift clinical emphasis in ways that influence downstream decisions so behavioural robustness with clinicians in the loop becomes part of the testing remit. Mandating task- and domain-based specifications can bridge this divide by mapping policy objectives to executable tests, informing quantitative risk thresholds or safety cases and accommodating differences in permissible tasks and user groups. Community-endorsed specifications would help developers choose architectures and training methods that balance robustness with accuracy, guide deployment teams in selecting prompt templates and calibrating user confidence and provide templates for failure reporting and incident management. Specifying robustness by priority grounded in realistic degradation mechanisms and task-critical metrics offers a scalable way to standardise evaluations, align with stakeholder risk and translate regulatory aims into practice. By adopting community-endorsed specifications that span knowledge integrity, population structure, uncertainty management and compound system behaviour, healthcare organisations can close the gap between laboratory performance and dependable deployment, improving safety while enabling responsible automation at scale. results.content: Published: 31 Oct 2022, Last Modified: 04 Aug 2025NeurIPS 2022 AcceptReaders: EveryoneShow BibtexShow Revisions Keywords: dataset shifts, scalp EEG, representation learning, healthcare machine learning, model robustness, latent space, uncertainty quantification, distribution shift TL;DR: We develop model diagnostic measures to identify failure modes of EEG-ML models before deployment without access to out-of-distribution data. We conduct experiments on multiple EEG feature encoders and two clinically relevant downstream tasks using publicly available large-scale clinical EEGs. Within this experimental setting, our results suggest that measures of latent space integrity and model uncertainty under the proposed data shifts may help anticipate performance degradation during deployment.
